To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

honeycomb core panel can be modelled as orthotropic material, the maximum load and stiffness can be predicted using the FEM method and the Tsai-Wu criterion is a good choice for modelling of the failure in honeycomb paperboard panels.
the honeycomb panel with regular hexagonal cells and with the real shape of the cell core can be modelled by using a finite element model with a good agreement with experimental results.
honeycomb-core panels are very sensitive to bending loads, and the maximum load and stiffness of such panels increase with the thickness of the panel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the flexural damage of honeycomb paperboards.
the numerical modelling of honeycomb paperboards and the experimental analysis of their mechanical properties.
the development of an experimental and numerical method for the prediction of damage and the failure of honeycomb paperboards.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FEM model of honeycomb panel with a real shape core cell and the use of failure criteria are very useful in predicting the maximum load and the stiffness of the panel.
the use of the finite element method in the analysis of the flexural properties of honeycomb paperboards is a useful tool for the design of honeycomb paper structures.
the numerical model of honeycomb paperboards with a regular shape of a hexagon is the most accurate and reliable one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible to use the FEM to model honeycomb-core panels and predict the failure of the panel by applying well-known failure criteria.
it was possible to predict the damage in honeycomb paperboard panels by using the numerical method.
a numerical model of a honeycomb paperboard can be successfully used to predict the maximum load and bending stiffness of a honeycomb panel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the Tsai-Wu failure criterion is the most effective in the analysis of the flexural damage of honeycomb paperboards, while the maximum stress criterion is the least accurate.
the use of the Tsai-Wu failure criterion in the FEM model of the honeycomb paperboard panel allowed for the prediction of its failure in the flexural test.
the numerical model can predict the behaviour of the honeycomb paperboard with high accuracy.
